changes.to: Issue #17 (2026-11-17): ToddlerBot - about 0.6 m and 2.7 kg, 30 active DoF (arms 7x2, legs 6x2, neck 2, waist 2), 0.25 m/s walking, lifts 1,484 g (about half its weight) per the Stanford project. ROBOTIS sells a US$4,335 parts bundle, not the robot, so no price is recorded; runtime varies (19 min under a walking policy before thermal limits). [replaced height_mm: 560 -> 600; weight_kg: 3.4 -> 2.7; payload_kg: 1.484 -> 1.5 | emptied (no maker value) runtime_h=0.32; price_usd=6000; price_note=list 6000 USD (maker), per HumanoidStore, checked 2026-09]
bill of materials under USD 6,000 for the open-source build (maker paper), not a sale price

Maker paper (CoRL 2025) and project site: 0.56 m tall, 3.4 kg, 30 active DOF excluding end effectors (7 per arm, 6 per leg, 2 neck, 2 waist), 2 fisheye cameras, IMU in the chest, speaker, 2 microphones, Jetson Orin NX 16GB, entirely 3D-printed with off-the-shelf Dynamixel motors, total BOM cost under USD 6,000, design under CC BY-NC-SA and code under MIT, with zero-shot sim-to-real transfer and a teleoperation interface; two end-effector designs (parallel jaw gripper and compliant palm) swap in two minutes. The catalog's earlier payload (1.484 kg), max speed (0.25 m/s) and runtime (0.32 h) were HumanoidStore figures that the maker paper does not state in those terms, so they were removed rather than kept on an aggregator's authority.
Open-source: Python library (pip installable), RL/DP training, teleoperation interface; design files under CC BY-NC-SA

changes.from: Compact humanoid from Stanford University; shipping now, anyone can order.
changes.to: ToddlerBot is Stanford's open-source, 3D-printed 56 cm humanoid for loco-manipulation research, with 30 active DOF, a Jetson Orin NX and a build cost under USD 6,000.
